title: Minimal CLI-first Stream API and Tool Sandbox — PRD (ideation)
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures an early PRD sketch for a minimal, CLI-first streaming API surface plus a local tool-sandbox runtime that lets engineers iterate on streaming + tool-calling flows without needing a full app or SDK integration. The goal is a low-friction onramp: developer types a short command, gets a streaming transcript with typed frames, and can flip on a local tool-simulator to validate tool-handshake behavior and structured outputs.

Problem / context:
- Many third-party engineering teams hit two friction points when evaluating our hosted streaming: (1) complexity of integrating SDKs and dealing with stream framing/partial JSON, and (2) difficulty in testing tool-calls (webhooks, DB writes, external APIs) because of remote network setup and auth.
- Existing hosted SDKs are powerful but overloaded for simple experiments — we want something you can run in 30s from a laptop.
- We also want reproducible deterministic replay for unit tests and integration checks (so product teams can assert structured output schemas across streaming deltas).

Primary users:
- Backend engineers prototyping LLM-driven automations who want a quick local loop.
- Mobile/web engineers validating incremental UI/UX while mocking tool responses.
- Solutions engineers doing POCs for customers (fast demo mode).

Goals (90-day / measurable):
1) Ship a CLI that can start a streaming session to hosted-api and output compact, typed frames to stdout (text, action, schema, checkpoint).
2) Provide a local "tool-sandbox" binary that receives tool-call frames and can be configured with simple mappings (e.g., when tool "search" called with q=*, return JSON), with support for scripted delays and failure modes.
3) Include deterministic session recording mode (replayable fixtures) so a session can be recorded and replayed locally for tests.
4) Add a minimal telemetry envelope in the CLI that emits session metrics to the Console for early analytics.

Non-goals (for first launch):
- Full language-specific SDKs (we will leverage existing SDKs in parallel).
- Complex GUI; this is terminal-first.
- High-scale load testing or multi-tenant sandboxing.

Success metrics:
- Time-to-first-stream: median time from download to first streaming token < 60s for new user.
- Number of sandbox sessions created by solutions/SEs in first 30 days >= 50.
- Deterministic fixture adoption: 10 internal tests converted to replay-based tests in first 90 days.
- Developer satisfaction: >4 (out of 5) on internal dev-experience survey.

High-level product flow:
1) Developer installs redwood-cli (npm/pip/homebrew binary).
2) redwood-cli login (token) 
3) redwood-cli stream --model redwood/fast-7b --prompt "fix this code" --sandbox ./sandbox-config.yaml
   - CLI opens a streaming connection to hosted-api.
   - Server emits typed frames (see frame types below) which CLI prints with minimal formatting.
   - When model emits a tool-call frame, redwood-cli POSTs the tool payload to local sandbox endpoint (default http://localhost:8765/tool) and prints the simulated tool response as a frame.
4) Developer toggles --record to save an event log (timestamps + frames) to a fixture file for replaying later.

Typed frame proposal (compact):
- text: incremental tokens or segments. payload: string
- tool_call: {tool: string, args: json-ish-string} 
- tool_result: {tool: string, result: json-ish-string} (emitted by sandbox or remote)
- schema_assert: {id: string, path: string, status: pass|fail, reason?} (optional inline assertions emitted by model/validators)
- checkpoint: session checkpoint id (useful to resume)

Important ergonomics notes:
- CLI should default to newline-delimited compact frames (one per line), with a --pretty flag to show colored, interactive view. Newline-delimited means easy piping: redwood-cli stream ... | jq -R -s '.' or pipe to replay.
- Tool sandbox config should be a tiny YAML with 
  - mappings: list of matchers -> responses
  - delays: optional per-mapping to simulate latency
  - failures: inject HTTP 500s or timeouts
- Sandbox should support an optional script mode: scripts are small JS/Python snippets that can transform inputs to outputs for richer behavior. Scripts run in a restricted environment.

API surface sketch (examples, not final):
- POST /v1/streams: body: {model, prompt, session_id?, output_schema?} returns 101/upgrade for streaming or streaming SSE with frames.
- Frames include: {t: "text" | "tool_call" | "tool_result" | "schema_assert" | "checkpoint", id: string, payload: string}
- Tool call semantics: when model emits tool_call frame, server delivers a tool_call event to registered webhooks or to sandbox via a proxy. Client can choose to auto-forward or pause until local ack.

Local sandbox CLI examples:
- sandbox-config.yaml:
  port: 8765
  mappings:
    - match: tool == "search" and args.q contains "redwood"
      response: {hits: ["doc1", "doc2"]}
    - match: tool == "create_ticket"
      script: ./scripts/create_ticket.js

- Command run: redwood-cli stream --model redwood/fast-7b --prompt-file example.md --sandbox sandbox-config.yaml --record ./fixtures/session-01.json

Deterministic replay model:
- When --record is enabled, CLI writes an event log with timestamps, frames, and local sandbox responses. Replay mode feeds frames back to the CLI (or to a test harness) preserving timing (or with --fast to strip delays). This allows CI tests that assert that sequence of frames contains specific schema_assert=pass.

Telemetry & observability:
- Lightweight envelope from CLI: session_id, model, start_time, duration, token_count, sandbox_injected_errors_count. This only activates if user is logged in and consented (telemetry opt-in).
- On server side, tag requests that used the CLI + sandbox for early cohort analysis.
- Provide a Console filter for "CLI sandbox sessions" so SEs can find demo sessions and troubleshoot.

Security & privacy:
- Sandbox is local by default; CLI will refuse to auto-forward tool calls to arbitrary remote URLs unless explicitly configured.
- Recorded fixtures must be marked explicitly as containing PII; provide an easy redact tool (redwood-cli redact fixtures --pii-map).

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal dogfood, 2 weeks): internal redwood-cli binary, sandbox scripts for SEs, 10 demo flows.
- Phase 1 (beta, 4 weeks): public binary, docs, two small tutorial notebooks, instrumentation to track adoption.
- Phase 2 (1–2 months): polish UX, add replay-first API hooks so CI can assert frames.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should tool-call frames be delivered to client as a single JSON blob or be chunked incrementally? Chunking helps large args but complicates local sandbox parsing. Prefer single atomized tool_call frame for V1.
- How much of the SDK behavior do we emulate in the CLI? We want parity in framing and handshake but not full retry semantics initially.
- Sandbox scripting: safe subset (JS with VM) vs small WASM-based runner. VM is quicker but requires sandboxing.
- Naming: CLI command name should be short and discoverable (redwood stream vs rwd stream).

Dependencies:
- Hosted-api streaming endpoint changes (frames + tool_call schema) — owning team: eng-hosted-api (HOSTED-987).
- Lightweight telemetry hook in Console to show CLI sessions — owner: console-and-rollouts.
- Minimal packaging pipeline for distributing redwood-cli (npm/homebrew/binary) — owner: developer-experience.

Next steps (owner/ETA):
- Product: finalize frame wire format and publish minimal spec (Avery, 2025-01-24).
- Eng: prototype sandbox binary and CLI streaming pipe (Marco, 2025-01-31).
- Docs: one-pager + quickstart for SEs (Priya, 2025-02-07).
- QA: define 5 canonical demo flows to record as fixtures (Jordan, 2025-02-07).

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments (informal):
- Could have a "playground mode" where CLI spins up a small web UI for visualizing frames, but initial focus is terminal.
- We should capture an "expectation file" for schema_asserts so a single CI assertion can validate end-to-end behavior.
- Consider quick integration with localtunnel/ngrok for remote webhooks in SE demos but default to disabled.

References / related tickets:
- HOSTED-987 (streaming frame changes)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/412 (frame contract sketch)
- Internal playbook: Stream CLI Sandbox Notes (confluence link in metadata)

End.
